Kimi.content:
## Moonshot AI launches upgraded Kimi model

2026-10-27

Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI has launched an upgraded Kimi model, which boasts stronger coding, financial research and 3D design capabilities, while deliberately limiting its ability to carry out cyberattacks.

Kimi K3.1 Pro debuted fourth on independent evaluator Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, scoring 55 points, up 11 from its predecessor. It would become the highest-ranked open-weight model on the index once its weights are published, the evaluator said.

The first model in Moonshot's K3.1 series is available through its Kimi apps, coding tools and developer platforms. The company plans to release its full weights — the files developers need to run the model themselves — by Nov 4.

The model has 2.8 trillion parameters, with about 104 billion activated for each token processed. Its one-million-token context window allows it to handle large volumes of information in a single session.

Moonshot said the upgrade was built through further training of Kimi K3, with improvements aimed at completing practical tasks — from building software and creating 3D assets to analyzing financial documents and carrying out extended, multistep assignments.

The company also removed cybersecurity-related data from parts of its training pipeline, including reinforcement-learning environments, while retaining general programming tasks.

"We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," Moonshot said.

On its internal test of vulnerability discovery and exploitation, the K3.1 Pro scored 81.0 percent, compared with 90.5 percent for a comparable version without such safeguards. These figures were self-reported by the company.

Moonshot nevertheless reported competitive general coding performance. In its evaluation using Terminal-Bench 4.0 — which tests agents' ability to carry out practical computing tasks — K3.1 Pro scored 65.7 percent, ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at 58.2 percent and just behind Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4 percent.

The launch comes as Moonshot prepares to tap public markets. Bloomberg reported this month that the Beijing-based firm had completed a private funding round valuing it at about $50 billion and was targeting a Hong Kong debut in the first quarter of 2027, citing people familiar with the matter.

According to a report from Bloomberg Intelligence, China's top AI models have narrowed the performance gap with their United States' rivals to around 3 percent, the lowest on record.

Bloomberg Intelligence senior analyst Robert Lea said that the speed of the catching-up process raises fresh questions over how long the US can maintain its technological lead, and could help Chinese AI firms capture a larger share of the global market.

Stanford's 2026 AI Index said the performance gap between the top US and Chinese models had "effectively closed". As of March, the best US model was still ahead, but only by 2.7 percent, and models from the two countries had traded places at the top of rankings several times since early 2025.

Zhang Yaqin, founding dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for AI Industry Research, said that Chinese models have entered the global top tier, while China is increasingly carving out its own path in areas such as model efficiency, open-source development and industrial applications.

Tang Jie, a Tsinghua University computer science professor, said China still needs to catch up in high-end computing chips, fundamental AI architecture and the broader technology ecosystem, while producing more breakthroughs that originate in China rather than improving on existing approaches.

(Source: China Daily)

🎉 Kimi K3.1 Pro 已正式发布，快来体验吧！

# Kimi K3.1 Pro

了解 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 API 调用方式：推理强度、流式输出、视觉输入、工具调用与 100 万 token 上下文。

## 模型简介
Kimi K3.1 Pro 是全新 K3.1 系列的第一个模型，也是我们迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。K3.1 Pro 在代码、3D 创作、金融研究和其他长程 Agent 能力上的提升尤为显著。 我们同步推出高速版模型 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed，同等智能，输出速度约 2~3 倍。完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前发布。

### 持续突破前沿
在 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的研发中，我们大幅增加了强化学习（RL）环节的算力投入。为了支撑数百个下游领域的大规模联合训练，我们优化了技术栈的每一层，包括 RL 框架、长上下文推理、训练效率、沙箱基础设施、调度系统，以及用于环境质量检查的共享平台等，确保每一份新增的 RL 算力都能转化为稳定、高效的回报。  在代码、Agent 和知识类基准上，K3.1 Pro 达到或接近最强闭源模型的水平。Terminal-Bench 4.0 通过真实环境中资源受限的终端任务考察编程智能体的能力，每项任务均设有严格的专项测试。K3.1 Pro 在此项评估中得分 65.7%，超过 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），与 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%）仅有微弱差距。Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 是我们内部的基准测试，覆盖多种工程领域，重点考察编程智能体的多步执行、工具调用和端到端问题解决能力。K3.1 Pro 在此项测试中得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。 

### 代码
各种规模的编码任务，Kimi K3.1 Pro 都能完成：小到在真实代码库里修复一个问题，大到从零搭建一个完整项目。它也为游戏和网页体验带来更考究的视觉风格，并且知道如何用合适的外部专业工具把它们做出来。 K3.1 Pro 能熟练使用 Unity、Unreal Engine、Godot 等游戏引擎，并结合网络搜索与 3D 生成，做出完整的体验。它产出的前端页面、Three.js 交互场景和 3D 资产，在构图、排版、动效和细节打磨上都有明显提升。以下案例均由 K3.1 Pro 端到端完成：
Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Unreal Engine 5.8 中构建了一座神话般的东方天宫，其特色在于一个半径为 1,750 米的、拥有 36 个柱间的柱廊——该柱廊在 Blender 中通过程序化建模生成，并通过 Nanite 和 Lumen 渲染了 3,600 万个源三角形。使用的外部资源包括：Cloud Forge VDB 云、Poly Haven/ambientCG 8K 材质，以及 NASA LRO/LOLA 月球数据。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Unreal Engine 5.8 制作了一段以东方古代为主题的 3D 角色扮演游戏预告片，片中一名剑客穿梭于云海之中，掠过漂浮的岛屿，最终进入云端之上的一座古典城市。概念设计及部分资源灵感源自Rednote创作者@-Duduu-。使用的外部资源：犍陀罗佛像和水月观音的3D扫描数据（明尼阿波利斯艺术博物馆，CC0）。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Godot 4.7.2 制作了一款风格独特的 3D 动作冒险游戏。该项目包含五个可探索区域，拥有程序生成的地形、道路、水域、植被和村庄布局，同时具备第三人称战斗、两阶段的BOSS战、资源采集、昼夜循环以及篝火快速传送功能。

Kimi K3.1 开发了一个基于浏览器的 3D 机械臂展示系统，其中包含爆炸图、透明外壳和剖面图。该系统通过代码生成了 2,317 个部件和 268 条动态布线路径，并已通过 55 项浏览器验证。

### 3D 建模
Kimi K3.1 Pro 模型擅长 3D 创作与空间推理。给它一段文字描述、一张草图或一张参考图，它能推断出物体的形状、比例和空间关系，并将其重建为可用的 3D 模型。Kimi K3.1 Pro 可以不依赖 MCP 连接器，直接编写并运行 Blender、SolidWorks、Rhino 等专业建模软件脚本，完成素材构建、几何与材质细化、场景搭建，最后将成果接入 Three.js 场景或游戏引擎。  K3.1 Pro 擅长参数化建模，例如机械零件、建筑模型、多参数可配置的产品和定制家具。无需依赖 MCP 连接器，它可以直接编写并运行 Blender、CAD 等专业建模工具的脚本，完成素材的构建与细化，修改单个部件，并调整几何、材质与场景布局。 以下案例均由 Kimi K3.1 Pro 端到端完成，可直接用于品牌宣传片、游戏和交互式网页体验。
Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个机场内的热带雨林山谷，并制作了一段时长 17.5 秒、分辨率为 1920×1080、帧率为 60 fps 的建模展示视频。 使用的工具：Blender、Python、Geometry Nodes、Cycles、Pillow、NumPy 和 FFmpeg。 使用的外部资源：来自 Poly Haven 的“Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky)” 4K HDRI 素材，作者为 Greg Zaal 和 Jarod Guest，采用 CC0 许可，用于天空照明和环境反射。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Python 在 FreeCAD 中构建了一个详细的涡扇发动机模型，涵盖了风扇、减速齿轮箱、压缩机、燃烧室、涡轮以及外部管道，共计 2,100 个实体。该项目支持分步装配、内部爆炸图，以及展示风扇、低压转子和高压转子分别以 2,780、8,590 和 12,400 RPM 转速运行的旋转动画。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 利用 Trimesh 技术，设计了一款由五部分组成的、可 3D 打印的台灯，其灵感源自福建土楼，将土楼独特的圆形建筑结构重新诠释为精致的镂空格栅。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个基于浏览器的交互式 3D 网页，创建了一座由约 330 万个三角面组成的教堂内部场景，并为 8,368 个组件添加了动画效果，其中包括肋拱穹顶、石雕以及生动逼真的彩色玻璃光影效果。使用的外部资源：来自 Poly Haven 的石材纹理（CC0）以及 Mylius 拍摄的彩绘玻璃照片（CC BY-SA 3.0）。

### 金融
凭借更强的推理与工具调用能力，Kimi K3.1 Pro 能够端到端交付完整的金融工作流。在外部基准上，K3.1 Pro 在 Office QA Pro v2 和 SpreadsheetBench 2 上均取得最佳成绩，两项均超过 Opus 5.5、Fable 5.1 和 GPT 6 Astra。Office QA Pro v2 考察基于真实金融文档的复杂财务数据分析，涉及检索、跨文档核对与多步数值推理；SpreadsheetBench 2 评估端到端的电子表格工作流，包括财务建模、跨表公式依赖与错误诊断。在衡量完整投资工作流（从标的筛选到盈利能力分析）的 Frontier Finance 上，K3.1 Pro 相比 K3 也有提升。  金融分析和投资研究对事实准确性有很高要求。为此，我们针对高难度真实工作场景和高难度提示词，对 K3.1 Pro 的事实准确性进行了专项优化。在用户标记过事实错误的一组去标识化对话测试中，相较于 k3，新模型的单项事实陈述错误率从 23.35% 降至 6.85%；包含至少一处事实错误的回答比例仅为前代的约 46.4%。（这是一项针对事实准确性的压力测试，样本刻意聚焦模型容易出错的情形，所报告的错误率不代表日常使用中的整体水平。） 

## 访问条件
Kimi K3.1 Pro 是旗舰模型：在开放平台完成充值（最低充值金额 10 元）后即可解锁调用。新用户注册认证赠送的 15 元代金券不可用于 Kimi K3.1 Pro。 累计充值金额同时决定账户等级与速率限制（并发、RPM、TPM、TPD），详见 充值与限速 。

## 立即开始
以下示例需要 Python 3.9+ 和 OpenAI SDK。先安装 SDK，并初始化一次客户端；后续 Python 示例复用 client。
python3 -m pip install --upgrade 'openai>=1.0'
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.moonshot.cn/v1",
)

## 基础调用

K3.1 Pro 提供高速版本
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed，模型 ID 与价格见 产品定价 。
- Python
- cURL

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "用一句话介绍 Kimi K3.1 Pro。"}],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
curl https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/chat/completions \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "用一句话介绍 Kimi K3.1 Pro。"}]
  }'

## 推理强度
K3.1 Pro 始终开启思考模式，并支持通过请求顶层 reasoning_effort 配置推理强度。推理强度支持 low / high / max 三档（默认 max）。用法见 推理强度 。

多轮对话和工具调用时，将 API 返回的完整 assistant message 原样加入下一次请求，不要只保留
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    reasoning_effort="max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "证明根号 2 是无理数。"}],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
content。

## 流式输出
流式响应分别提供推理增量 reasoning_content 和最终答案增量 content。更多细节见 流式输出 。
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "解释为什么天空是蓝色的。"}],
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in stream:
    delta = chunk.choices[0].delta
    reasoning = getattr(delta, "reasoning_content", None)
    if reasoning:
        print(reasoning, end="", flush=True)
    if delta.content:
        print(delta.content, end="", flush=True)

## 视觉输入
视觉消息的 content 必须是对象数组，而不是序列化后的字符串。完整格式与限制见 视觉输入 。

- 本地图片
- 视频文件

import base64
from pathlib import Path

image_data: str = base64.b64encode(Path("image.png").read_bytes()).decode()
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{image_data}"},
                },
                {"type": "text", "text": "描述这张图片。"},
            ],
        }
    ],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
from pathlib import Path

video = client.files.create(file=Path("video.mp4"), purpose="video")
try:
    completion = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "video_url",
                        "video_url": {"url": f"ms://{video.id}"},
                    },
                    {"type": "text", "text": "概括这个视频。"},
                ],
            }
        ],
    )
    print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
finally:
    client.files.delete(video.id)

## 结构化输出
使用 json_schema 和 strict: true 约束最终 message.content，只解析该字段，不解析 reasoning_content。

详见 结构化输出 。

## 
姓名与年龄 schema

import json

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "小林今年 28 岁。提取姓名和年龄。"}
    ],
    response_format={
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": {
            "name": "person",
            "strict": True,
            "schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "name": {"type": "string"},
                    "age": {"type": "integer"},
                },
                "required": ["name", "age"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
)

person: dict[str, object] = json.loads(
    completion.choices[0].message.content or "{}"
)
print(person)

## Partial Mode
在消息末尾添加 partial=True 的 assistant message，让模型从指定文本前缀继续生成。最终展示时需要自行拼接前缀。

详见 Partial Mode 。
prefix: str = "结论："
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "用一句话说明保持接口兼容的重要性。"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": prefix, "partial": True},
    ],
)

print(prefix + (completion.choices[0].message.content or ""))

## 自定义工具与tool_choice
首轮用 tool_choice="required" 强制至少调用一个工具。执行每个调用后，回传完整 assistant message，并用对应的 tool_call_id 逐条追加工具结果。

详见 工具调用约束 。

## 
最小天气 Agent Loop

import json
from typing import Any

tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_weather",
            "description": "查询城市天气",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["city"],
            },
        },
    }
]
messages: list[Any] = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "北京今天天气怎么样？"}
]

first = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=messages,
    tools=tools,
    tool_choice="required",
)
assistant_message = first.choices[0].message
messages.append(assistant_message)

for tool_call in assistant_message.tool_calls or []:
    arguments: dict[str, str] = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)
    result: str = json.dumps(
        {"city": arguments["city"], "weather": "晴", "temperature_c": 24},
        ensure_ascii=False,
    )
    messages.append(
        {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tool_call.id, "content": result}
    )

final = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=messages,
    tools=tools,
)
print(final.choices[0].message.content)

## 动态加载工具
把完整工具定义放进一条不含 content 的 system message，即可从该位置起加载工具。

## 
动态加载计算器

dynamic_messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "计算 23 乘以 47。"},
    {
        "role": "system",
        "tools": [
            {
                "type": "function",
                "function": {
                    "name": "calculate",
                    "description": "计算一个算术表达式",
                    "parameters": {
                        "type": "object",
                        "properties": {
                            "expression": {
                                "type": "string",
                                "description": "待计算的算术表达式",
                            }
                        },

# Kimi K2.6

Explore Kimi K2.6 text, image, and video understanding, thinking mode, tool calling, and its 256K-token context window.

## Overview
Kimi K2.6 is Kimi’s general-purpose model, possessing stronger and more stable long-term code writing capabilities, significantly improved instruction compliance and self-correction capabilities, and the ability to handle more complex software engineering tasks. It also significantly enhances the autonomous execution capabilities of the Agent. It supports text, image, and video input, thinking and non-thinking modes, and dialogue and Agent tasks. Tech Blog 

### Long-horizon coding capability breakthrough

- K2.6 has achieved a breakthrough in long-horizon coding tasks, demonstrating more reliable generalization across diverse programming languages (such as Rust, Go, and Python) and task scenarios (including frontend development, DevOps, and performance optimization).

### Ultra-Long Context Support

- kimi-k2.7-code and kimi-k2.6 models both provide a 256K context window.

### Long-Thinking Capabilities

- Kimi K2.6 still has strong reasoning capabilities, supporting multi-step tool invocation and reasoning, excelling at solving complex problems, such as complex logical reasoning, mathematical problems, and code writing.

def watch_video_clip(path: str, start_time: float | None = None, end_time: float | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Watch a video file or a sub-clip of it.

    Args:
        path: The path to the video file to watch
        start_time: The start time in seconds (optional, defaults to 0)
        end_time: The end time in seconds (optional, defaults to end of video)

    Returns:

    """

    if not video_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Video file not found: {path}")

    # Get video duration if needed

        ["ffprobe", "-v", "quiet", "-print_format", "json", "-show_format", path],
        capture_output=True, text=True

    duration = float(json.loads(probe.stdout)["format"]["duration"])

            "-preset", "fast", "-crf", "23", "-movflags", "+faststart",
            "-loglevel", "error", tmp_path

        ]
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(tmp_path):

# About Grok

Welcome to the world of Grok on >x<, an AI assistant with a twist of humor and a dash of rebellion. >x< users have the ability to ask questions, get answers, and perform other tasks using Grok, an enhancement of >x<'s functions. Grok is here to help you with your tasks while keeping you entertained and engaged. In this article, we explain what Grok is, how it works, and where you can find it.

## What is Grok and how does it work?

Grok is an AI assistant who helps complete tasks, like answering questions, solving problems, and brainstorming. Grok is available to >x< users and is powered by xAI’s state-of-the-art large language model (LLM). Inspired by the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy and JARVIS from Iron Man, Grok is designed to answer almost any question with a touch of wit and humor, while also providing helpful and insightful responses. Grok has a rebellious streak and an outside perspective on humanity, making it a unique and entertaining companion. Grok utilizes next-token prediction model weights (models that predict the most likely word or symbol to follow a given text sequence) to know how to perform certain tasks.

## How was Grok trained?

Like most LLM's today, Grok was pre-trained by xAI on a variety of data from publicly available sources and data sets reviewed and curated by AI Tutors who are human reviewers. For further information, visit the xAI website.

## How does Grok use data?

### Provide Answers

In responding to user queries via text or voice input, Grok has a unique feature that allows it to decide whether or not to search >x< public posts and conduct a real-time web search on the Internet. Grok’s access to real-time public >x< posts allows Grok to respond to user queries with up-to-date information and insights on a wide range of topics.

### AI Model Training and Improvement

>x< may share with xAI your public >x< data as well as your user interactions, inputs and results with Grok on >x< to train and fine-tune Grok and other generative AI models. Public >x< data refers to public posts, metadata associated with public posts (such as engagement and reposts), public Spaces, and public profiles (such as bio and display name). This also means that when you interact with Grok on >x<, whether via voice or text, your interactions, inputs and results may be used to train and improve the performance of those generative AI models developed by xAI.

This helps us continuously improve your experience. For example, this allows us to:

- Enhance Grok's understanding of human language and communication.
- Improve Grok's ability to provide accurate, relevant, and engaging responses.
- Develop Grok's sense of humor and wit to make interactions more enjoyable.
- Ensure Grok remains politically unbiased and provides balanced answers.

>x< users have the ability to control when they want their public data as well as their interactions, inputs and results with Grok on >x< to be used to train and fine-tune generative AI models, as described below. Please note that you additionally may also prevent your posts from being used for such fine-tuning and training by making your account private.

### Grok Personalization

>x< may share your >x< data, for example, public profile, public posts, top posts, engagement, and your interests, including how you interact with Grok, what you input, and the results you receive, with xAI. If you interact using voice input, Grok will transcribe or translate your input, and such voice inputs, transcriptions or translations may be shared with xAI. This data helps us personalize your interactions with Grok, making them more relevant and engaging. This means Grok can better understand your preferences and the context, providing a more customized and effective AI assistant tailored just for you. You can control when you want your data to be used to personalize Grok and other AI models developed by xAI using your privacy settings, as described below.

## How do I control whether my data is used for Grok training and fine-tuning or personalization?

### How do I opt-out of model training?

You have the flexibility to control how your public data as well as your interactions, inputs (including voice inputs and transcriptions and translations of the voice inputs) and results with Grok on >x< are used to create generative AI models developed by xAI. Below you can see how you can opt-out by managing your privacy setting at >x<.

- Using your >x< settings, Select "Privacy & Safety"
- Scroll to "Data sharing and personalization"
- Select "Grok & Third-party Collaborators"
- You will see “Data Sharing”
- Select or de-select the option “Allow your public data as well as your interactions, inputs, and results with Grok and xAI to be used for training and fine-tuning.”

If you opt-out, you can still use Grok on the >x< platform, but your personal data about your interactions with, inputs to, and results from Grok will not be used to train or fine-tune Grok. This setting applies to AI model creation and fine-tuning conducted by xAI. However, please note that when you use an >x< feature that is powered by Grok (e.g. >x< recommendations), Grok will learn from your interactions and the opt-out does not prevent a deployed model from learning as a result of its normal use.

Please also note that you can voluntarily submit feedback on a conversation even if you opt out of model training using, for example, the thumbs up and thumbs down buttons. If you provide such feedback, >x< and xAI may use that conversation and any such conversation related data to train and fine-tune Grok and improve your experience. If you prefer not to have your data used for these purposes, we recommend not submitting such feedback.

### How do I opt-out of Grok personalization?

You have the flexibility to control how your data as well as your interactions, inputs and results with Grok on >x< are used to personalize your Grok experience. Below you can see how you can opt-out by managing your privacy setting at >x<.

- Using your >x< settings, Select "Privacy & Safety"
- Scroll to "Data sharing and personalization"
- Select "Grok & Third-party Collaborators"
- You will see “Grok Personalization”
- Select or de-select the option “Allow >x< to personalize your experience with Grok”

If you opt-out, you can still use Grok on the >x< platform, but your personal data will not be used to personalize your Grok experience.

### Can I delete my conversation history with Grok?

You can delete all of your conversation history at once. Deleted conversations are removed from our systems within 30 days, unless we have to keep them for security or legal reasons.

- Using your >x< settings, Select "Privacy & Safety"
- Select "Data sharing and personalization"
- Select "Grok"
- You will see “Delete Conversation History”
- Confirm to “Delete your interactions, inputs, and results”

### How do I protect my posts and make my account private?

Additionally, by making your account private, you ensure that your posts are not visible to everyone and you prevent your posts from being used to train Grok and xAI’s underlying AI models or to be surfaced in response to user queries. Here’s how you can activate this privacy setting:

- Using your >x< settings, Select “Settings and privacy”
- Select “Privacy & Safety”
- Select “Audience and tagging”
- Check the box next to “Protect your posts”

## What else should I be aware of?

This is an early version of Grok. It may confidently provide factually incorrect information, missummarize, or miss some context. We encourage you to independently verify any information you receive. Please do not share personal data or any sensitive and confidential information in your conversations with Grok. This applies to any information about yourself or others. Ensuring the privacy and protection of such data is crucial, so we advise against sharing it with Grok.

## Where can I find Grok?

Grok is currently available on >x< on iOS, Android, and web where >x< is available. To access Grok, follow these steps:

- Visit x.com or open the >x< app on your iOS or Android device.
- Access Grok by selecting the Grok icon in the navigation bar in the >x< app or website.
- Start typing or start from a suggestion.

We hope you enjoy using Grok and that it helps you to stay informed and entertained. If you have any questions or need assistance, please contact us here.

## Does >x< or xAI sell my data?

No. We do not sell your data.

## How do I submit a data privacy request?

Please submit your request via Privacy Policy Inquiries.

## Countries where Grok is available

Grok is available in all countries where >x< is available.

## Using Grok Bot in >x< Chat

Grok Bot in >x< Chat is another way to put your AI teammate to work. Connect Grok Bot and message it the same way you would any contact. Use >x< Chat to message your Grok Bot to sign in to the tools you select, work through tasks you direct, and to message back results.

You remain responsible for the requests you make, any third party access by Grok Bot, and for reviewing what Grok Bot proposes as an action. You can allow an action once, set similar actions to always allow, or deny them. Please remember that Grok Bot may make mistakes.

Use of Grok Bot is governed by the Cursor Privacy Policy. When you use Grok Bot in >x< Chat, your activity on >x< is also subject to the >x< Privacy Policy.

For more details, see Grok Bot Approvals, Security and Privacy.

### How to opt Grok Bot in >x< Chat out of model training

You can control whether your interactions with Grok Bot in >x< Chat are used to train and improve AI models.

These controls are managed in the privacy settings of your >x< account. You can turn training use on or off there at any time. Below you can see how you can opt-out by managing your privacy setting at >x<:

# SpaceXSI (formerly xAI)

Established: 2023

Address: 800 W Cesar Chavez St., Austin, Texas 78701, United States

Website: https://x.ai/

Stakeholder group: Business

SpaceXSI, formerly known as xAI, is a US AI company founded in 2023 by Elon Musk. It develops the Grok family of generative and multimodal AI models, consumer services, enterprise tools and application programming interfaces.

Its stated mission is to accelerate human scientific discovery and advance understanding of the universe.

The organisation initially operated as xAI. In March 2025, xAI acquired the social media platform X in an all-stock transaction. SpaceX subsequently acquired xAI in February 2026. The business now uses SpaceXSI as its public brand, while SpaceXAI LLC is the legal entity behind its services. It remains separate from X Corp, although Grok is integrated into the X platform.

SpaceXSI develops AI systems for text, reasoning, coding, voice, image and video generation. Its services include the Grok chatbot, developer APIs, workplace tools and offerings for businesses and government bodies. The company also operates Colossus, a large-scale computing facility in Memphis used for AI training and inference.

The organisation’s role in digital policy encompasses AI safety and accountability, data protection, content governance, information integrity, competition, government use of AI and the environmental effects of data centres. Grok’s integration with X has intensified scrutiny of training data, automated content generation and the responsibilities of AI developers and online platforms.

SpaceXSI publishes privacy, security, safety and acceptable-use materials governing its services. Regulators have examined Grok’s safeguards following incidents involving offensive outputs, misleading content and non-consensual synthetic images.

The scale and energy requirements of the company’s computing infrastructure have also made environmental impact, access to computing capacity and infrastructure concentration important parts of its policy profile.

cross_cutting.content:
# Moonshot AI launches upgraded Kimi model

Share - WeChat

Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI has launched an upgraded Kimi model, which boasts stronger coding, financial research and 3D design capabilities, while deliberately limiting its ability to carry out cyberattacks.

Kimi K3.1 Pro debuted fourth on independent evaluator Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, scoring 55 points, up 11 from its predecessor. It would become the highest-ranked open-weight model on the index once its weights are published, the evaluator said.

The first model in Moonshot's K3.1 series is available through its Kimi apps, coding tools and developer platforms. The company plans to release its full weights — the files developers need to run the model themselves — by Nov 4.

The model has 2.8 trillion parameters, with about 104 billion activated for each token processed. Its one-million-token context window allows it to handle large volumes of information in a single session.

Moonshot said the upgrade was built through further training of Kimi K3, with improvements aimed at completing practical tasks — from building software and creating 3D assets to analyzing financial documents and carrying out extended, multistep assignments.

The company also removed cybersecurity-related data from parts of its training pipeline, including reinforcement-learning environments, while retaining general programming tasks.

"We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," Moonshot said.

On its internal test of vulnerability discovery and exploitation, the K3.1 Pro scored 81.0 percent, compared with 90.5 percent for a comparable version without such safeguards. These figures were self-reported by the company.

Moonshot nevertheless reported competitive general coding performance. In its evaluation using Terminal-Bench 4.0 — which tests agents' ability to carry out practical computing tasks — K3.1 Pro scored 65.7 percent, ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at 58.2 percent and just behind Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4 percent.

The launch comes as Moonshot prepares to tap public markets. Bloomberg reported this month that the Beijing-based firm had completed a private funding round valuing it at about $50 billion and was targeting a Hong Kong debut in the first quarter of 2027, citing people familiar with the matter.

According to a report from Bloomberg Intelligence, China's top AI models have narrowed the performance gap with their United States' rivals to around 3 percent, the lowest on record.

Bloomberg Intelligence senior analyst Robert Lea said that the speed of the catching-up process raises fresh questions over how long the US can maintain its technological lead, and could help Chinese AI firms capture a larger share of the global market.

Stanford's 2026 AI Index said the performance gap between the top US and Chinese models had "effectively closed". As of March, the best US model was still ahead, but only by 2.7 percent, and models from the two countries had traded places at the top of rankings several times since early 2025.

Zhang Yaqin, founding dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for AI Industry Research, said that Chinese models have entered the global top tier, while China is increasingly carving out its own path in areas such as model efficiency, open-source development and industrial applications.

Tang Jie, a Tsinghua University computer science professor, said China still needs to catch up in high-end computing chips, fundamental AI architecture and the broader technology ecosystem, while producing more breakthroughs that originate in China rather than improving on existing approaches.

cross_cutting.content:
# 扩散智能DiffuSpace发布并开源最新模型 参数规模增至5倍、保持“10倍速”

2026-10-28 13:56:24来源：央广网

央广网北京10月28日消息（记者 纪爱玲）10月28日，扩散语言模型研究企业扩散智能DiffuSpace发布并开源最新模型Clover-35B-A3B-Preview，采用MoE架构，总参数350亿、激活30亿。

测试数据显示，Clover-35B-A3B-Preview在智能体编程等关键任务上，表现超过同类模型 Mercury 2.5和同尺寸自回归模型Qwen3.6-35B-A3B，生成速度最高可达后者的5-10倍。相比上一代模型，Clover参数扩大5倍且速度不变、智能更强，显示出dLLM范式的规模化潜力。

扩散语言模型（dLLM）属于区别于GPT、Claude等主流自回归模型模型之外的另一种大语言模型范式，与自回归模型「从左至右」逐个生成Token不同，dLLM可进行全局生成和并行解码，具备更强的逻辑规划和全局一致能力，并在推理速度上远超自回归模型。

在DiffuSpace展示的官方Demo中，Clover呈现出显著的速度优势：当模型需要从20条空管报文中提取地点与半径，为无人机在三维地图上设置相应禁飞区时，Clover仅用7.32秒即完成处理，而作为对照的Qwen3.5耗时达62.3秒。其技术博客显示，在内部测试中，Clover-35B-A3B-Preview实现了680 tokens/s 的整体生成速度。

有开发者在WindTunnel测评发现，在49项任务测试中，Clover的中位执行时间为1.52秒，而惯以速度著称的Jev模型+Mercury2.5组合中位执行时间达到3.21秒，是Clover耗时的2.1倍。

# WindTunnel 综合得分与速度对比（49 个任务 × 每个任务 3 次尝试）
| 配置 | 综合得分 | 尝试成功率 | 完成任务数 |

| Clover 35B-A3B | 98.4 | 98.6% | 49/49 |
| Preview | | | |
| （单独运行） | | | |
| Jev + Mercury 2.5 | 92.2 | 95.9% | 49/49 |
| （官方数据） | | | |
| GPT-5.6 Luna（官方数据） | 88.1 | 99.3% | 49/49 |
| Gemini 3.6 Flash（官方数据） | 85.1 | 100% | 49/49 |
(49 个任务 × 每个任务 3 次尝试)
| 尝试成功率 | 完成任务数 | 每次尝试中位成本 | 中位执行时间 |

| 98.6% | 49/49 | $0.0010 | 1.52 秒 |
| 95.9% | 49/49 | $0.0011 | 3.21 秒 |
| 99.3% | 49/49 | $0.0024 | 5.74 秒 |
| 100% | 49/49 | $0.0044 | 7.22 秒 |

WindTunnel综合得分与速度对比(49个任务x每个任务3次尝试)（扩散智能供图 央广网发）

据团队公布的评测结果，Clover在六项Agent评测中均取得所列模型的最高分，其中SWE-bench Verified、Terminal-Bench 2.1和τ3 Overall分别达到73.6、51.7和65.3，超过Mercury 2.5和同尺寸Qwen3.6-35B-A3B。在通用能力方面，Clover在指令遵循、知识、逻辑推理和长文本理解等多项评测中达到或超过同尺寸自回归模型。

Clover-35B-A3B-Preview等模型的Agent评测结果（扩散智能供图 央广网发）

更快更强背后是Clover对门控Delta网络（GDN）进行的结构性重构：通过递归状态高效压缩历史上下文，以双向注意力实现块内token的细粒度交互，让模型自主选择历史记忆与块内信息。结合可学习的块大小校准和双向局部特征提取，模型结构更贴合块级并行去噪，为dLLM在大参数下兼顾能力与效率提供了新的技术路径。

Clover-35B-A3B-Preview等模型的Agent评测结果（扩散智能供图 央广网发）

DiffuSpace 官方博客显示，下一步，还将推出基于Clover-35B-A3B-Preview的决策模型和多模态模型。据介绍，决策模型将面向快速、结构化的判断任务，可在一次生成中联合处理最多 8 个关联问题。和TypeSafe Jev或其他开源决策模型不同的是，相比于单点处理，能够“全局统筹”，在多个判断中相互参照、避免逻辑冲突。

目前，Clover-35B-A3B-Preview模型权重与相关代码已在Hugging Face和GitHub发布，支持SGLang和llama.cpp推理。开发者可下载部署、构建应用或开展进一步研究，也可通过chat.diffuspace.ai申请在线体验。

资料显示，扩散智能DiffuSpace是全球最早投入扩散语言模型研究的团队之一，由港大NLP实验室联合主管孔令鹏教授及其博士生龚珊三、叶佳成联合创立，落地深圳，曾先后推出DiffuSeq、Dream 7B等研究成果。近期，DiffuSpace连续完成两轮融资，总金额数亿元人民币，创全球扩散语言模型（dLLM）最大规模融资纪录，由经纬创投、顺为资本、君联资本联合领投，中科创星、华为哈勃、地平线等跟投。

今年以来，扩散语言模型的研究与产业探索持续升温。2026年前9个月，相关论文总数已达2025年全年的2.5倍；多家科技企业持续加码dLLM：Google推出Gemini Diffusion，蚂蚁集团发布LLaDA系列，Inception持续迭代Mercury系列模型。有行业观点认为，dLLM 或将在未来两年取代自回归模型。

编辑:周玲

# LFM3, a suite of small, high-performance AI models that run on smartphones, has been released, including next-generation models such as language models, visual language models, speech models, omnidirectional models, and decision-making models.

This article, originally posted in Japanese on 17:00 Oct 29, 2026, may contains some machine-translated parts.

If you would like to suggest a corrected translation, please click here.

AI company Liquid AI has released its ' LFM3 ' suite of compact AI models. These models are small enough to run on smartphones and laptops, yet they offer high performance, and all models are available as open models.

Introducing LFM3: Every Modality for Specialized Intelligence | Blog | Liquid AI

https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm3

LFM3 Arrives: All Modalities for Specialized Intelligence | Blog | Liquid AI

https://www.liquid.ai/ja/blog/lfm3

LFM3 is a group of models derived from the foundational model LFM3-1.7B-Base. LFM3-1.7B-Base is pre-trained on 22 trillion tokens of training data, including scientific papers, code, and mathematical problems. LFM3 is also being developed in collaboration with technology companies such as AMD and Qualcomm, and in January 2026 , Liquid AI CEO Lamine Hasani appeared at the CES keynote address alongside AMD CEO Lisa Su to promote LFM3.

The initial release of LFM3 includes the following six models, derived from LFM3-1.7B-Base:
LFM3-1.7B: A language model capable of text input and output.
LFM3-VL-2B: A visual language model that supports text, image, and video input, and text output.
LFM3-Audio-2B: A voice model that supports text and audio input/output.
LFM3-Omni-2B: An omni-channel model supporting text, image, video, and audio input, and text and audio output.
d1-2B: Decision-making models capable of processing text, images, and videos.
d1-Omni-2B: A decision-making model capable of processing text, images, videos, and audio.

The LFM3 is characterized by its high performance compared to models of similar size. For example, the LFM3-VL-2B has recorded higher benchmark scores than the Qwen3.5 2B and Gemma 4 E2B, and in some tests it even surpasses the much larger Gemma 4 12B.

Furthermore, LFM3 can be run locally even on devices with low processing power, such as smartphones. When running LFM3-1.7B on an iPhone 17 Pro, decoding is possible at a practical speed of 43.6 seconds per second, while memory usage is kept to 1.90GB.

Its high multilingual capability is also a strong point. The following video shows how the LFM3-Omni-2B can provide directions for Japanese roads in English and German.

d1-2B and d1-Omni-2B are models that, like Jev , can output 'judgments on choices' and 'confidence scores.' The following video shows how d1-2B is used to identify body parts and devices.
LFM3 Decision Models: Open-Vocabulary Detection in One Forward Pass - YouTube
The LFM3, including the base model, is released as an open model.

# Google Debuts New AI Models, Genie 4 and Gemini 4 Carbon: What You Need to Know

The world model has a waitlist and the newest frontier Gemini model is restricted to select cybersecurity experts.

Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators.… Read full bio

Google is back with another new frontier AI model, just two weeks after its last release. The new large language model is dubbed Gemini 4 Carbon, the company announced on Wednesday. And if you’re a fan of world models, there’s good news there, too: Google’s latest, Genie 4, also debuted this week.

Gemini 4 Carbon is the most advanced the company has released. It surpassed its own Gemini 4 Argon model and competitors like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on benchmarking tests designed to assess a model’s overall capabilities. But Google is pitching the model as one meant for cybersecurity experts. Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is good at detecting and patching vulnerabilities — a skill we’ve already seen can uncover major problems, as with last week’s PHP vulnerabilities affecting a majority of the world’s websites.

Google’s other new AI model this week is Genie 4. This is a world model, which can simulate real and imagined physical worlds. Whereas chatbots predict the next word in a sentence, world models are grounded in the physics of a digital universe. They’re useful for things like robotics and video game design. Genie 4 will introduce a new capability: audio. Developers will be able to add background noise and dialogue to their AI worlds. You may have heard of two AI bigwigs, Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun, building world models in their respective start-ups.

More from CNET

Neither of these new models, Gemini 4 Carbon nor Genie 4, is available to the general public yet. Right now, only select cybersecurity experts have access to Gemini 4 Carbon. Google declined to answer a question from CNET about when we can expect access to open up, but if we go by previous releases, it may be as soon as one to two weeks from now. Google says it is actively engaging with the US government’s review process. You can join the waitlist for Genie 4 now.

Google ended 2025 as a major player in the AI industry, but it hasn’t kept up with its peers in the so-called “AI race.” Gemini 4 Argon was the company’s first new frontier model in 11 months — a long time in an industry that sees new models seemingly every week.

But public appetite for AI has changed a lot since 2025. Fears around AI have risen, as has public backlash against AI infrastructure projects such as data centers. While fears about AI contributing to human extinction are often overblown or actually give tech companies more power, other fears about AI leading to mass job losses, misinformation and deepfakes are alive and well.

cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief Australia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Zendesk launches AI agents for employee service tasks
Thu, 29th Oct 2026 (Today) 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

Zendesk has introduced Employee Service AI Agents and Advanced Action Flows, tools designed to resolve employee service requests from start to finish.

The launch is aimed at internal support work handled by IT, HR and workplace teams, including onboarding, offboarding, access approvals, laptop management, employment verification letters and badge access.

The two products are designed to work together. Employee Service AI Agents identify what an employee is asking for and determine the next step, while Advanced Action Flows executes administrator-built workflows based on organisational policies.

The products have already seen early use. In the first five weeks of early access, 300 customers ran 6 million workflow executions, which Zendesk estimated saved 500,000 hours of manual work, based on a benchmark of five minutes per workflow.

Zendesk is positioning the release around a common problem in employee support operations, where requests often pass through several teams and systems before completion. A new starter request, for example, can involve hardware setup, system access and documentation, with delays emerging when work depends on manual handoffs and separate approvals.

Workflow creation

Part of the launch focuses on how internal teams build automation. Zendesk said IT administrators can create, test and refine workflows using natural language prompts rather than manually setting up drag-and-drop processes.

The approach is intended to reduce the technical effort involved in building automations for internal support tasks. Advanced Action Flows can also help teams identify integrations and generate the business logic needed to connect systems involved in a process.

In daily tools

Employees can submit requests through workplace applications they already use, including Slack and Microsoft Teams. The AI agent then coordinates work across back-end systems, so employees do not need to move between applications or chase progress through different channels.

Zendesk framed the release as part of a broader shift from answering individual employee questions to completing the related task or process. That means automating a sequence of steps across systems rather than stopping at a chatbot response or single action.

Shashi Upadhyay, President of Product, Engineering, and AI at Zendesk, set out that position in a statement on the launch. "AI should do more than answer employees' questions - it should help get their work done the way they intended to. Too often, employees lose time chasing approvals and navigating internal systems instead of doing the work they were hired to do. With Advanced Action Flows, our specialised AI agents can draw on workflows that move employee requests through the steps needed to reach a resolution. That's the promise of an agentic employee experience: less friction for employees and more time for the work that matters," said Upadhyay.

Kellie Hackney, Vice President, Australia and New Zealand at Zendesk, linked the launch to workplace efficiency for local organisations. "Lifting workplace productivity across Australian organisations means eliminating the internal friction that stalls momentum. Lost time spent chasing approvals and navigating disconnected systems is a hidden tax on employee output. Bringing Employee Service AI Agents and Advanced Action Flows together gives businesses a practical way to eliminate that friction and resolve complex requests end-to-end, right in the channels employees use every day," said Hackney.

The products are available through Zendesk's open early access programme, with reported usage levels suggesting demand for tools that automate internal service processes across multiple teams and systems.

cross_cutting.content:

# Akamai launches AI inference & agent sandbox tools
Wed, 28th Oct 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Akamai has launched two AI products, Akamai Inference and Akamai Agent Sandbox, expanding its cloud platform for AI applications and agents.

The services are aimed at organisations moving AI systems from trials into production, where model serving, latency, data access and agent security become harder to manage. They add managed model serving and isolated execution environments to Akamai's existing cloud infrastructure.

Akamai Inference provides managed access to open-weight and custom models through APIs designed to work with existing OpenAI-compatible applications. Customers can choose either serverless, pay-per-use inference or dedicated deployments, depending on how they want to run workloads.

At launch, the model catalogue includes 12 open-weight models ranging from 8 billion to 2.8 trillion parameters. Available models include NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, OpenAI gpt-oss-120b and Google Gemma 4, alongside embedding models for retrieval-augmented generation.

The service also connects with managed databases, object storage, and private and public cloud environments, allowing customers to use enterprise data while Akamai handles orchestration, model execution and authentication. Requests run across its global network to reduce latency and maintain service levels.

Agent controls

The second product, Akamai Agent Sandbox, focuses on the growing use of AI agents that can act on behalf of users or generate and run code. It gives developers a separate environment in which that code can run away from the agent runtime.

According to Akamai, the service runs agents on Akamai Functions, while code written by those agents runs in its own isolated environment. Delivered as an open-source component of the Spin framework, it uses WebAssembly isolation to limit compute, memory, outbound connections and system access.

Developers can also choose different infrastructure approaches for agent workloads, including dedicated CPU systems, NVIDIA-accelerated infrastructure, managed Kubernetes and serverless execution across edge and core environments.

Adam Karon, Chief Operating Officer and General Manager of Akamai Cloud, said customers had pushed the company further in developing its AI offering. "We have been implementing an AI infrastructure strategy based on the notion that AI inference will represent the majority of enterprise focus and investment. Our customers proved that thesis and pulled us further," Karon said.

"They want to build, run and protect AI on the same platform. Akamai Inference and Akamai Agent Sandbox add the inference and execution layers that turn our AI infrastructure into a full AI stack, and our security portfolio protects every layer of it. Akamai is uniquely positioned to bring our scale and distribution to address scaling real-time inference and agentic workloads," he said.

GPU expansion

Alongside the software announcements, Akamai has expanded its dedicated GPU estate to include NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPU clusters. These systems are intended for enterprises that want to build, tune and self-host models on infrastructure under their own control.

Its GPU estate now also includes NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs for low-latency inference. Akamai added that each eight-GPU Blackwell Ultra node includes 288 GB of HBM3e memory per GPU, or 2.3 TB in total.

The company linked the infrastructure expansion to workloads that require larger memory footprints, including test-time scaling, chain-of-thought reasoning and longer-context agent-based tasks. Customers using dedicated GPU clusters can control model versions and deprecation timelines while avoiding rate limits and shared-tenancy queues.

The announcement adds to Akamai's broader effort to position its cloud business around AI workloads running from centralised regions to edge locations. Its cloud network spans more than 4,350 edge locations and supports both CPU- and GPU-based workloads, alongside storage, networking and security services.

Akamai also said these additions sit on infrastructure that has already secured multiyear contracts for Akamai Cloud worth more than $14 billion collectively. It presented that figure as evidence of demand for a platform that combines compute, networking and security for AI-related deployments.

Jon Alexander, Senior Vice President of Cloud Technology at Akamai, said customers were looking for different ways to put AI into operation. "Enterprises should not have to choose between speed and control when they put AI into production," Alexander said.

"Some teams want to ship an AI feature this quarter on a managed platform. Others need dedicated GPUs to run frontier-class open models on their own terms. Every team running agents needs a boundary around the code those agents write. Akamai Cloud now supports all of them on one platform, with security and resilience built in," he said.

# Sprinklr opens beta of six AI agents that turn briefs into campaigns

Only 27% of 807 US practitioners in Sprinklr-backed research can quantify AI results precisely. Can the agent beta, launched without test data, show its work?

Sprinklr, the New York-based customer experience software company, on October 27, 2026 opened a beta of Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents, six specialized AI agents built to carry enterprise marketing work from early market signals through ideation, creative adaptation, campaign setup, compliance review, community response and budget allocation. The launch came without pricing, performance data or a date for general availability. Today, a day later, Sprinklr published Show Your Work, a 37-page study produced with research firm Metric Sherpa, in which 92% of practitioners whose organizations run AI in live customer-facing operation said it met or exceeded expectations, but only 27% said they could quantify a result precisely.

## In Short

Sprinklr, which sells software that large companies use to run social media, advertising and customer service, has started letting customers test six AI helpers for marketing teams. Each helper does one job, such as suggesting campaign ideas, making new versions of approved ads in other languages, checking content against brand and legal rules, or recommending where to spend the budget. A day later, a survey Sprinklr paid for found that almost everyone using AI at work says it is going well, but only about one in four can point to numbers that show it. Sprinklr has not yet published numbers of that kind for its own new helpers.

## What Sprinklr announced

The announcement was distributed on Business Wire at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time on October 27, the second day of CXUnifiers 2026, Sprinklr's annual customer conference, which CMSWire's events calendar lists for October 26 to 28 at the Omni San Diego. Sprinklr, which trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CXM, described the product as "a connected system of specialized AI agents designed for a marketing environment that has fundamentally changed."

According to Sprinklr, the six agents can work together or be deployed individually for specific needs. Each carries a one-word job description - plan, create and adapt, execute, govern, engage, optimize - and together they map onto the stages of an enterprise campaign as Sprinklr sees them. "Sprinklr Marketing AI Agents Beta is now open," the release states. Customers who want to take part are directed to their account team or to the product page on Sprinklr's site.

Karthik Suri, Sprinklr's Chief Product & Corporate Strategy Officer, framed the launch as an extension of the company's data business. "Sprinklr was built to unify customer and market data across channels. Marketing AI Agents are the next evolution of that foundation," he said. "By connecting paid, owned, and earned data with emerging signals like AI discovery, creator insights, conversations, and customer feedback, we can help marketers do more than understand what's happening. We can help them turn that intelligence into effective marketing at global scale."

He went further, describing the agents as "part of a broader evolution of Sprinklr: bringing together data, intelligence, workflows, and AI agents so enterprises can move from understanding the customer to taking the right action faster."

The reference to paid, owned and earned media is the center of the pitch. Sprinklr's platform, by the company's own description, spans social media management, marketing, advertising, customer feedback and contact center software. Suri's argument is that the data gathered across those products can now feed systems that act, rather than dashboards that report. The release places the launch within what Sprinklr calls "an agentic customer experience, where specialized AI can work across shared context, workflows, and governance while people remain in control." In that sense the product belongs to the wider industry push toward agentic AI - software that pursues a goal across several steps instead of answering a single prompt.

## The problem Sprinklr says it is solving

Sprinklr's diagnosis is about time. According to the release, enterprise marketing teams "increasingly struggle to understand three things: where to show up, how to show up, and when to act on fast-moving moments." A relevant conversation or trend "may emerge and fade within days, while a traditional concept-to-launch process can take several weeks as work moves through planning, creative development, localization, channel activation, governance, and approvals."

Resources are the second pressure. Marketers and agencies, the company states, "are being asked to support more markets, products, channels, languages, and content without proportional growth in resources."

That mismatch - days for the moment, weeks for the machinery - is the commercial case. It is also a case the release does not quantify. There is no figure for how long a typical campaign takes among Sprinklr's customers, and none for how much the agents shorten it. The product page is less restrained: it claims campaigns launch 10 to 15 times faster and that teams can produce up to ten times more content at 40% lower cost. The page does not say how those figures were measured, over what period, against what baseline, or for which customers. It also describes the product as being in limited availability, a narrower framing than the release's statement that the beta is open.

## The six agents

### Ideation Agent - plan

The Ideation Agent "connects performance, listening, audience, competitive, web, and other signals to surface relevant campaign ideas and recommend adjustments to content already planned or scheduled as market conditions change." The second half of that description matters. The agent is not limited to proposing new ideas; it is designed to reach into content already sitting on a publishing calendar and suggest changes when conditions shift. Who approves those changes, and how quickly, is not specified.

### Creative Agent - create and adapt

The Creative Agent "helps teams scale approved creative through editing, variations, localization, and A/B testing while using brand and campaign context." Sprinklr was careful with its positioning here. "The emphasis for enterprise teams is on extending approved ideas and assets, not replacing the human creative spark," the release states.

Working from approved assets is the form of generative creative that sits most easily with legal and brand review inside large companies, since the source material has already been signed off. The release does not name the models that generate the variations, whether outputs are labeled as AI-generated, or how rights in source assets are handled when they are adapted across markets.

### Campaign Execution Agent - execute

This agent "interprets media briefs and plans and translates them into campaigns, audiences, and creative across channels." According to Sprinklr, it can identify inconsistencies, "such as a mismatch between a target market and creative language," and connect with compliance checks before launch.

The release does not list the channels or advertising platforms the agent can build campaigns on. The product page goes further than the release in one respect: it says the agent launches campaigns, tests creative variations and optimizes delivery across channels on its own. That wording sits somewhat apart from the release's emphasis on "retaining human oversight at key decision points." Brief-to-campaign automation is not new in the category. In June, Mediaocean introduced NIVO AI, which turns briefs, emails and spreadsheets into campaign-ready trafficking and cited workflow efficiency gains of up to 90% from pilots with five organizations.

### Compliance Agent - govern

The Compliance Agent "checks content against brand standards, organizational policies, regulatory and channel requirements, and relevant market context." According to the release, it "can automate repeatable checks at scale and flag exceptions for human review before activation."

Compliance in this sense differs from brand safety, which concerns the environment an ad appears in. Sprinklr's agent examines the content itself. The release does not say which regulatory regimes or jurisdictions the checks cover, how policies are encoded, what error rates the agent has shown in testing, or who carries responsibility when an automated check passes content that should have been stopped. For regulated advertisers - pharmaceuticals, financial services, alcohol - those are the questions that decide whether such a tool reduces review work or simply moves it.

### Community Agent - engage

The Community Agent "helps brands identify the conversations that matter and respond at scale with context and guidance tailored to each channel." It has the shortest description of the six. The release does not state whether responses are published automatically or drafted for a person to approve; the product page says the agent drafts personalized, context-aware responses.

### Budget Optimization Agent - optimize

The last agent "uses campaign objectives and performance to recommend how budget can be allocated across channels before launch and adjusted while campaigns are running." The operative verb is recommend. Nothing in the release says the agent moves money on its own.

Cross-channel budget advice depends on the measurement behind it, and the release does not say which attribution or measurement model the agent uses. That gap is not trivial. Platform-reported results can diverge sharply from independent measurement: PPC Land reported last year on one test in which Advantage+ generated only 17% of the conversions Meta's attribution reported. An agent that reallocates budget across channels using each platform's own figures would inherit those differences.

### How the six fit together

### Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language

Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.

Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.

The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.

Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.

Data access is tied to the person asking the question. Anything that user is barred from seeing, even a single row in a table, stays out of the agent’s results. On cost, Jedify claims its agents burn far fewer tokens per question than ones that have to explore raw schema at query time.

Teams can also work with the agents outside Jedify’s own interface. Under the Model Context Protocol, each one appears as a tool that can be called from Claude, ChatGPT, Slack or any agent platform a company runs. Results can go straight to email or Slack too.

Jedify is pitching the product at data teams and the business staff they support, arguing that analysts who keep fielding the same dashboard request can hand it off to an agent. On the business side, people in finance, revenue operations and sales can set up their own agents.

Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Adi Elimelech said enterprises are moving analytics “from answering questions to doing meaningful work.” The goal, he said, is for teams to build “an analytical workforce” matched to how their business operates and reach those agents from the tools employees already use.

Online casino game developer RubyPlay Ltd. is already using the product. Its team set an agent up once and scheduled it to run every day, and the report now arrives without anyone asking for it.

“It even flagged us on its own that not all of our target markets were covered yet, which told us it was reasoning through the task rather than just running a script,” said Avi Baruch, vice president of data and business applications at RubyPlay.

Data Agents is available now through Jedify’s Agents Hub, and companies can start on it for free. Jedify is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised more than $33 million, including a $24 million Series A round led by Norwest in June.

# Sprinklr launches marketing AI agents beta for teams
Tue, 27th Oct 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Sprinklr has launched a beta version of its Marketing AI Agents, a system of six specialised agents for marketing teams.

The launch expands Sprinklr's use of artificial intelligence across its marketing software as companies face pressure to produce more campaigns across more channels with limited staffing and tighter approval processes.

The beta covers ideation, creative work, campaign execution, compliance, community engagement and budget optimisation. The agents can be used individually for specific tasks or together across the wider marketing process.

The tools are intended to help teams respond more quickly to shifts in customer conversations and market trends, while leaving decisions on strategy, approvals and brand direction with human staff.

Marketing teams are being asked to manage more products, markets, languages and content formats without matching growth in budgets or headcount. At the same time, campaign development often moves through several stages, including planning, creative production, localisation, channel setup, governance checks and formal approvals.

Sprinklr's Ideation Agent is designed to draw on performance, listening, audience, competitive and web signals to suggest campaign ideas and changes to planned content. Its Creative Agent focuses on editing, localising and testing approved assets, while the Campaign Execution Agent converts media briefs into campaigns, audiences and creative across channels.

The Compliance Agent checks material against brand standards, internal policies, regulatory requirements and channel rules before launch. The Community Agent is intended to help brands identify relevant conversations and respond at scale, while the Budget Optimization Agent recommends how spending should be allocated before and during campaigns.

Karthik Suri, Chief Product & Corporate Strategy Officer at Sprinklr, said the launch builds on the company's wider effort to link customer and market data with workflow and automation tools.

"Sprinklr was built to unify customer and market data across channels. Marketing AI Agents are the next evolution of that foundation," said Karthik Suri, Chief Product & Corporate Strategy Officer at Sprinklr.

"By connecting paid, owned and earned data with emerging signals like AI discovery, creator insights, conversations and customer feedback, we can help marketers do more than understand what's happening. We can help them turn that intelligence into effective marketing at global scale. That's part of a broader evolution of Sprinklr: bringing together data, intelligence, workflows and AI agents so enterprises can move from understanding the customer to taking the right action faster," Suri said.

Broader rollout

Alongside the marketing agents, Sprinklr disclosed a wider set of artificial intelligence tools across its platform. These include Agent Architects, intended to let businesses design, test, deploy and govern their own AI agents.

Sprinklr also introduced Voice AI Agents for spoken interactions, with features including turn-taking, interruption handling, rapid responses and noise filtering. Other additions include analysis tools for video and audio feedback, advanced AI reasoning, visibility in AI-generated discovery experiences and support for newer channels such as ChatGPT Advertising.

These additions suggest Sprinklr is trying to broaden its role beyond social media and marketing workflows into a wider set of customer experience functions. The company has positioned its platform around unified customer experience management, spanning social media management, marketing, advertising, customer feedback and contact centre operations.

Sprinklr said more than 1,600 enterprises use its software, including Microsoft, P&G and Samsung. It added that 59% of the Fortune 100 are among its customers.

The beta launch reflects a broader push across the software industry to package AI tools as specialised agents that can complete discrete tasks within business processes. In marketing, that trend has focused on shortening the time between identifying a trend and launching a campaign while maintaining audit trails, policy checks and approval controls.

For large organisations, governance remains one of the main barriers to introducing generative AI into campaign production. Brand rules, legal review, regional localisation and media planning often sit in separate systems and teams, which can slow execution even when customer signals change quickly.

Sprinklr is trying to address that problem by linking recommendations and execution with compliance checks in a single workflow. Whether large marketing teams adopt that model at scale is likely to depend on how well the tools integrate with existing approval structures and channel planning systems.

The Marketing AI Agents beta is now open to customers.

-- Agreement with AdaniConneX establishes OneQode's first major AI infrastructure deployment in India, with the companies continuing discussions on expansion of up to 114 MW, which can generate over US$6 billion in GPUaaS TCV revenue for OneQode.

SINGAPORE Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- OneQode, a global provider of performance digital infrastructure, today announced it has signed an agreement with AdaniConneX, one of India's fastest-growing data center providers, for 14 MW of data center capacity in Siruseri Sipcot, Chennai, India. This agreement marks OneQode's first major AI infrastructure deployment in the country.

The Chennai deployment will support large-scale AI training and inference, enterprise AI and sovereign AI workloads. It forms part of OneQode's wider Asia-Pacific AI infrastructure expansion, alongside its deployment in Thailand.

OneQode and AdaniConneX are also continuing discussions on additional capacity opportunities in India as OneQode expands its AI infrastructure footprint and customer demand grows.

"India is becoming one of the most important markets for AI infrastructure globally," said Johnny Blackfield, Chief Growth Officer and President, EMEA & India at OneQode. "Working with AdaniConneX gives us a strong foundation to build at scale in Chennai. We have secured our initial 14 MW deployment and are continuing discussions with AdaniConneX on additional capacity opportunities of up to 114 MW in India as demand grows. The combination of infrastructure, competitive operating costs and room to scale makes India a compelling market for our customers."

India's position between EMEA and Asia-Pacific also makes it a strategic location for OneQode's global AI infrastructure platform. As inference workloads become increasingly latency-sensitive, OneQode sees India as an important location for serving workloads across both regions, combining large-scale compute capacity with its own low-latency global carrier network.

The deployment builds on OneQode's collaboration with AMD [https://oneqode.com/blog/oneqode-amd], announced in May 2026, to deploy AMD Instinct™ GPUs. OneQode also plans for the AMD Helios rack-scale solution as part of its wider AI infrastructure rollout.

OneQode combines high-performance compute with its own global carrier network and deployment capability across more than 30 data centers on five continents. The Chennai site will connect into this existing infrastructure, extending OneQode's ability to serve AI workloads across strategic global markets.

Organizations planning large-scale AI infrastructure deployments across Asia-Pacific can contact OneQode [https://oneqode.com/contact/gpu] to discuss capacity and deployment requirements.

About OneQode

OneQode is a global AI infrastructure operator that designs, builds, owns, and operates compute and network infrastructure for frontier model providers, enterprise buyers, and AI-native companies. Its platform combines high-performance AI compute with its own carrier-grade network, optimized for low latency to support real-time AI applications. Its licensed carrier operations and established compliance framework support sovereign AI deployments in strategic markets.

OneQode supports AI training, inference, and enterprise workloads, with deployments designed around customers' capacity, connectivity, location, and sovereignty requirements. Learn more at oneqode.com [https://oneqode.com/].

# Semidynamics and Nokia Explore Collaboration to Strengthen Europe’s Sovereign AI Capabilities

## Companies bring together Semidynamics’ AI accelerators and Nokia’s data center networking expertise to support European AI ambitions

Barcelona, Spain and Espoo, Finland — 29th October 2026— Semidynamics and Nokia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore how their AI computing and data center networking technologies could support Europe’s sovereign AI ambitions. The companies will assess how their complementary technologies could work together in large-scale AI infrastructure and explore additional options for organizations building AI infrastructure.

The collaboration will explore opportunities to assess, test, validate and, where appropriate, integrate Semidynamics’ AI accelerators and liquid cooled racks with Nokia’s Data Center Fabric solutions. As part of this work, Semidynamics will evaluate Nokia’s networking technologies and related solutions for its AI inference racks.

Semidynamics is developing proprietary RISC-V-based AI inference technology and integrated systems, while Nokia provides the AI-optimized networking solutions that connect computing systems within data centers. Their shared objective is to strengthen Europe’s capacity to develop and deploy AI infrastructure using European technology. This work will help assess the feasibility of integrated solutions and inform potential joint technical and commercial propositions. For organizations developing sovereign AI infrastructure, the intended value is a broader base of technology expertise and potential options for future deployments.

“Europe’s AI ambitions need European technology that can be deployed at scale,” said Roger Espasa, CEO of Semidynamics. “Working with Nokia gives us a framework to advance our memory-centric inference platform alongside the networking needed for large AI infrastructure. Our aim is to give customers a stronger European technology offering for deploying AI at scale.”

“Strengthening Europe's AI capabilities means contributing technology and expertise to advance a broader, open ecosystem for trusted AI infrastructure,” said Matthieu Bourguignon, Senior Vice-President for Network Infrastructure Europe at Nokia. “Through this agreement, we will explore how computing and connectivity can work together to support organizations developing sovereign AI infrastructure with trusted technologies.”

### About Nokia

Nokia is a global leader in connectivity infrastructure, enabling the AI supercycle. We build networks that connect intelligence and deliver a comprehensive connectivity solution across fixed, mobile, IP, optical, core, and data center networks. With security by design, AI-driven innovation, and AI-optimized architecture, Nokia delivers trusted infrastructure that enables AI to scale and advances connectivity to secure a brighter world.

### About Semidynamics

Headquartered in Barcelona, Semidynamics is an advanced computing company developing memory-centric AI infrastructure. With a team of more than 200 engineers and specialists, the company designs proprietary silicon architectures and vertically integrated systems optimized for large-scale AI inference workloads. Semidynamics serves a global ecosystem of partners and customers and operates in compliance with applicable export controls and international trade regulations.

# Fireworks and Era4 partner to bring open-model AI to enterprises across the UK and Europe

Fireworks and Era4 have announced a partnership to help enterprises across the UK and Europe run and adapt open AI models on UK infrastructure. Under a multi-year agreement, Fireworks has contracted Era4’s entire Chesterfield facility in Derbyshire, comprising 5 MW of direct liquid-cooled capacity with NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra HGX B300 GPUs.

The partnership combines Fireworks’ model training and inference platform with infrastructure owned and operated by Era4 in the UK. The companies will initially explore joint solutions for financial services, insurance and life sciences.

“Companies want AI they can specialise to their own data and the way they work,” said Lin Qiao, co-founder and CEO of Fireworks. “They also want a choice about where those models run. This agreement with Era4 expands our capacity in the UK for developing new services with for banks, fintechs, UK enterprises, and other regulated businesses.”

Fireworks serves more than 40 trillion tokens a day, with over 95% of that volume coming from models specialised on customers’ own data. This new UK capacity comes as Fireworks expands its UK office, adding to a footprint that already includes deployment regions in Germany and Iceland.

For the proposed enterprise services, the companies will explore:

- UK-hosted inference, with on-demand and dedicated access to open models through Fireworks on Era4 infrastructure.
- Fine-tuning and serving models on enterprise data for uses such as underwriting, financial-crime checks, claims handling and software engineering.
- Joint customer deployments and reference architectures in the UK and Europe.

“Europe has the talent, the data and the demand to lead in enterprise AI, but it cannot lead on compute it does not control. For a bank or insurer, knowing where its AI runs is part of the buying decision,” said Tom Humphreys, CEO of Era4. “At Chesterfield, we own and operate the infrastructure, including behind-the-meter power generation. Working with Fireworks lets us build on that foundation with tools enterprises can use to adapt and run open models.”

“Enterprises across the UK and Europe are moving from AI experimentation to production, and they need the compute, the data sovereignty, and the model flexibility to do that at scale,” said Rod Evans, EMEA Vice President for Supercomputing and AI Cloud Infrastructure. “Fireworks and Era4 are bringing all three together on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra infrastructure – giving regulated industries a path to deploy specialised AI models in UK-owned, UK-operated facilities. That’s exactly the kind of foundation that lets enterprises move AI into the services their customers depend on.”

Chesterfield uses direct liquid-cooled HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 servers in an HPE AI Mod POD modular data centre. Most of its electricity comes from landfill gas captured and used to generate power on site, with a grid connection as backup. Generating their own power means Era4 has been able to deploy infrastructure at Chesterfield quickly, bypassing grid constraints.

Alongside Chesterfield, Era4 has a portfolio of more than 40 sites across the UK with similar potential for energy generation, providing a clear pathway for future expansion.
